title: Private upgrade toolchain & migration gates for VPC/on‑prem
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: This ticket defines and implements a deterministic upgrade toolchain for Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) that supports orchestrated data and schema migrations, LTS/patch channel semantics, and rollout gates for safe canary and staged upgrades. The scope covers the upgrade controller (operator), migration orchestration plan, versioning policy, rollout gate implementations (healthchecks, metric thresholds, manual hold), upgrade artifacts and signing for air‑gapped installs, and runbooks for rollback and emergency fixes.

Motivation: Customers running Private expect predictable upgrades across isolated networks and strict compliance windows. We must provide a tested, auditable upgrade path that: (1) safely applies control-plane and runtime changes including database migrations; (2) respects LTS patch policy and minor/major upgrade rules; (3) allows staged rollout with automated health and quality gates; (4) supports offline (air‑gapped) deployments with signed bundles and manifest compatibility checks.

Design overview:
- Versioning model: adopt semver-like tags but introduce a stable LTS channel label (e.g., private-2026.LTS-1) and a patch-only semantic variant for emergency fixes. Upgrade controller must enforce allowed version jumps: patch-only within LTS, minor jumps within same minor allowed with migration hooks, major requires manual approval.
- Upgrade controller (redwood-private-upgrade-controller): Kubernetes operator that coordinates the upgrade across components: control plane, operator CRDs, runtime nodes, and stateful services (Postgres, object storage migrations). It performs: preflight checks, staged rollout (canary -> cohort -> full), migration orchestration ordering, state snapshotting, and postflight validation.
- Migration toolchain: declarative migration manifests with idempotent tasks (schema migrations, kv transforms, index builds, config migration). Each migration has metadata: id, target_version, estimated_downtime, reversible: true|false, rollback_instructions_url. Migrations run in a controlled transaction/lock window when possible; long-running transforms run on background workers with progress reporting.
- Rollout gates: health-based automatic gates (service readiness, error budget consumption, 95th p50/p95 latency deltas, request success rate), data-consistency gates (replica sync), and manual hold gates for regulatory windows. Gate thresholds configurable per-customer via Private config with sane defaults.
- Air‑gapped upgrades: artifact bundles include signed manifests, checksums, and a bootstrap offline installer. Controller supports applying local bundle and verifying signature via customer KMS/HSM integration or a pre-shared signing key.
- Observability & traceability: every upgrade run emits structured events to customer audit logs and Redwood Console (when connected), with a unique upgrade run id, per-step timestamps, metrics snapshots, and links to CI artifacts/GitHub PRs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Upgrade controller prototype coordinates a canary -> cohort -> full rollout for a 1->2 node cluster with a reversible migration.
- Declarative migration manifests can be applied independently of controller for manual runs.
- Automatic health gates stop and rollback to previous stable revision when success rate drops below 99% or error budget exceeds configured thresholds.
- Air‑gapped bundle installation completes end‑to‑end in a lab environment and verifies signatures.
- Documentation: runbook, operator CRD spec, sample migration manifests, compatibility matrix, rollback playbook published to Confluence.

Out of scope: full multi‑datacenter orchestration, third‑party database engine conversions (e.g., Postgres->CockroachDB). Those will be tracked in follow‑up tickets.

Risks and mitigation:
- Long-running schema migrations may block runtime. Mitigation: prefer nonblocking transforms, background copy+swap pattern, and add migration time estimates and throttles.
- Rollback complexity for irreversible migrations. Mitigation: mark migrations reversible flag and require manual approval for irreversible ones; provide pre-upgrade snapshot guidance.
- Air‑gapped signature management complexity. Mitigation: provide two options (customer-managed signing with HSM or Redwood-signed bundles for enterprise customers under an SLA).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+Upgrade+Toolchain
- Operator prototype repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrade-controller/pull/58
- Migration manifest examples: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/private-migrations-examples
- Observability dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade-run-dashboard
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+Upgrade+Runbook

Next steps:
1) Finalize CRD contract and migration manifest schema (owners: Elliot, Maya).
2) Implement preflight checks library and sample checks for Postgres health, disk headroom, KV cache integrity (owner: Elliot).
3) Build canary orchestration flow and gating logic with metric hooks (owner: Sofia).
4) End‑to‑end lab test with air‑gapped bundle (owner: QA team).
comments: 2026-03-02 Sofia Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes added; primary goals and success criteria reviewed with Release Eng, SRE and PM. Action: Elliot to sketch CRD fields by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-05 Elliot Ng: Draft CRD schema pushed to the prototype repo (PR #42). Key fields: upgradeRunId, targetVersion, migrationSetRef, canarySpec, gateConfig. Need feedback from storage team for migration locking semantics.

2026-03-06 Maya Patel (SRE): Raised concern about running heavy migrations during business hours. Suggested default throttle policy and an option to schedule migrations during maintenance windows. Added label 'maintenance-window' to ticket.

2026-03-08 Design review (Ana Rodriguez): UX for manual gates in Console considered. Suggested adding 'hold reason' and 'expected duration' fields to make on-call handoffs clearer. Design will provide mockups by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-10 PR feedback (ENG): Reviewed rollback hooks — added explicit snapshot step before irreversible migrations. Also added progress reporting API for long transforms so Console can show percent complete.

2026-03-11 QA: Ran canary flow in lab cluster with synthetic traffic. Canary passed basic health gates, but p95 latency spiked during index build migration. Action: add index-build throttling and increase gate window to 15 minutes.
2026-03-13 Security: Confirmed that air‑gapped signing flow requires documented customer key onboarding steps. Security will draft key exchange and verification guidance by 2026-03-18.
